title: Automate Gong call follow-up with Glean Triggers in n8n
description: Use the Glean Trigger node in n8n to summarize a Gong call, log it in Salesforce, and post a Slack heads-up.

questions.prompt: Will you use n8n Cloud or a local/self-hosted n8n instance? If local/self-hosted, choose a public HTTPS option before importing: n8n's development --tunnel, Cloudflare Tunnel, or another public ingress. Glean cannot deliver to localhost.
What is your work email? It is used once to discover your Glean tenant and normalized API backend.
Where should the follow-up go in Slack? Start with one channel id, or provide a Salesforce Account id → Slack channel id map if each account team has its own destination. Use ids, not names.

verification.expectedDuration: 5–15 minutes after a test Gong call is indexed

prerequisites: Glean Triggers enabled with the Gong preset available, Gong calls indexed, and credentials scoped for Triggers, Search, and Chat
A publicly reachable n8n instance, or a local one exposed with npx n8n start --tunnel
Permission to install the Glean n8n community nodes
Salesforce and Slack credentials with the required write access

demoQueries.query: Finish a Gong call involving the trigger owner and a customer with a matching Salesforce Account
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: The workflow summarizes the call, creates one completed Salesforce activity on the matched Account, and posts the summary and source link to the configured Slack destination.

codeAssets.description: Importable n8n workflow plus an offline structural verifier

steps.title: Choose n8n hosting before scaffolding
steps.description: Choose n8n Cloud or local/self-hosted n8n before downloading anything. Cloud is public by default. Local/self-hosted needs a public HTTPS webhook origin—use n8n's development `--tunnel`, Cloudflare Tunnel, or another ingress, and keep it available before publishing.

steps.title: Resolve the Glean backend
steps.description: Run the cookbook resolver with the work email. It may see a legacy frontend address such as `*.askscio.com`, but it returns the API backend `https://<instance>-be.glean.com`. Use that result for Glean Chat; do not paste the discovery address into the workflow.

steps.title: Install the Glean n8n nodes
steps.description: In n8n, open Settings → Community nodes → Install and add `@gleanwork/n8n-nodes-gleanclient@0.4.2`. It provides the Trigger and Search nodes; the workflow uses an HTTP Request for Chat. Cloud works as shipped. For self-hosted n8n, set the webhook base to your public origin or start the development tunnel.

steps.title: Import the workflow
steps.description: In n8n, choose Workflows → Import from File and select the scaffolded `workflow.json`; this is the route that keeps your local edits. Import from URL always fetches the untouched GitHub file. If your browser cannot see the scaffolded file, copy and paste it onto a blank canvas. Confirm that the ten nodes and Start here note appear.

steps.title: Attach credentials
steps.description: Attach a Glean Trigger credential with `TRIGGERS`, a Glean Client credential with `SEARCH` and `CHAT`, plus your Salesforce and Slack credentials. The trigger follows the Glean credential owner; there is no separate user to select.

steps.title: Configure Glean Chat and Slack routing
steps.description: Set the Glean Chat node to the backend returned by the resolver, then choose one reviewed Slack channel or an Account-to-channel map. n8n Variables can hold the backend and routing values, but they are optional.

steps.title: Verify the workflow with no credentials
steps.description: Run the fixture verifier against recorded data. If you edited the local workflow.json, run `npm run verify:config` too. That command cannot see values entered in the n8n UI or stored in n8n Variables, so verify those configurations inside n8n before publishing.

steps.title: Publish the workflow
steps.description: Publish the workflow in n8n. The Glean Trigger node registers the production webhook and stores the signing secret used to verify deliveries.

steps.title: Verify with a real Gong call
steps.description: Make a short Gong call with yourself as a participant. Confirm one execution, one completed Salesforce activity on the matched Account, and one Slack post. Read the summary before widening the audience.

aiPrompt: Before downloading the workflow, ask whether the user will use n8n Cloud or local/self-hosted n8n. For local/self-hosted, require a public HTTPS webhook origin before publishing; offer n8n's development --tunnel, Cloudflare Tunnel, or another public ingress, and never accept localhost as reachable by Glean. Ask for the user's work email, then run the cookbook plugin's resolve-backend.mjs script and use its normalized https://<instance>-be.glean.com result for the Glean Chat URL; do not paste a legacy *.askscio.com discovery URL into the workflow. For trigger concepts or endpoint details, consult https://developers.glean.com/guides/triggers/overview and https://developers.glean.com/api/platform-api/triggers-overview. Scaffold the shipped n8n workflow, install exactly @gleanwork/n8n-nodes-gleanclient@0.4.2, and attach host-managed credentials rather than writing secrets into JSON. Keep the live Glean preset selected by semantics, not only by cached id. Configure either one reviewed central Slack destination or a reviewed Account-to-channel map. Preserve the single-account gate and the completed Salesforce activity pattern. Run the offline workflow verifier, publish only after every credential and mapping is configured, then verify one real Gong call end to end.
llmContext: The published Glean n8n package is 0.4.2. It includes a Glean Trigger node and a Glean Search action, not a Glean Chat node. The trigger registers POST /api/triggers on activation, stores the returned signing secret, verifies Standard Webhooks delivery, and deletes the trigger on deactivation. Glean event payloads are thin, so retrieve permission-aware context before summarization. n8n credentials must remain host-managed. Do not write to Salesforce or Slack if the account is absent, ambiguous, or unsupported by evidence.

content.problem:
Important follow-up gets lost after customer calls—not because the information is missing, but because it is scattered across Gong, Salesforce, and Slack.

This recipe connects those systems in n8n. When a new Gong call is indexed, Glean finds permission-aware context and summarizes it, Salesforce gets an activity only when one account matches, and Slack receives a focused update for the right audience.
takeItFurther: Create Salesforce follow-up tasks from explicit call action items, so every commitment has an owner.
Send a daily digest of completed and unresolved follow-ups instead of one Slack post per call.
Route unresolved accounts to a human review queue once that ownership path is in place.

guardrails.title: One account or no write
guardrails.rule: The workflow writes only after exactly one Salesforce Account matches. Ambiguity stops the run instead of choosing for you.

guardrails.title: Evidence before summary
guardrails.rule: The summary uses the call and permission-aware Glean results. Unsupported commitments, dates, and pricing stay out.

limitations.title: Account matching still needs a review path
limitations.description: Glean Chat proposes the customer from the call context, but Salesforce remains the authority. The workflow continues only when exactly one Account matches; otherwise it stops for resolution.
